I am a 35-year-old farmer in Quzhou County, and I have been working my family’s land since I left middle school. I farm about 7 mu of flat, irrigated land at the edge of our village. Like my father and grandfather before me, I stick to the wheat–maize double-cropping system because it is the most reliable way to feed my family and earn cash from the grain station. My winter wheat is already in the ground from last October; right now it is greening up, and I will top-dress urea at the jointing stage and irrigate three times before harvest in early June. Seed and fertilizer costs have gone up, so I use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed to get the best yield for my money. I do not waste money on deep ploughing—rotary tillage is fast and good enough for our soil. After the wheat comes off, I will immediately plant summer maize and irrigate twice during its growth. I spray pesticides when I see insects or when my neighbors start spraying, usually twice per crop. I expect my wheat to yield around 500 kg per mu and the maize about 600 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.
